newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Teachers' pay pushes NZ labour costs up in Mar yr.
newsitem.headline: Teachers' pay pushes NZ labour costs up in Mar yr.

text.p: Large increases in teachers' salaries helped to push New Zealand labour costs up in the year to March, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Thursday.

Salary and wage rates (including overtime) were 2.2 percent higher in the March 1997 quarter than the year-ago quarter, following rises of 1.9 percent and two percent for the years to September and December respectively.
A rise of 0.7 percent in each of the latest two quarters contributed to the annual rise.
"It is six years since quarterly increases this high were recorded," SNZ said.

"Increases in the salaries of teaching professionals and in the salaries of managers at primary and secondary schools caused one-fifth of the latest quarterly and annual increases in salaries and wage rates."

Public sector salary and wage rates rose 2.9 percent in the year to March, following a rise of 2.5 percent in the year to December. Within the sector, salary and wage rates rose 3.1 percent in central government and 2.1 percent in local government.

Growth in the private sector also turned up, after easing slightly in the second half of last year. The latest annual increase was two percent, returning to the level recorded in the year to June 1996, after edging down to 1.9 percent and 1.8 percent in the years to September and December.
The private sector rise was broadly based, with 12 of the 19 industry groups having higher annual rises this quarter than last.
SNZ said insurance and financial services led the private sector rise for the quarter, up 1.1 percent.
Base salary and ordinary time wage rates in all sectors were on average 2.2 percent higher in the March quarter than a year ago, up from a two percent annual rise the previous quarter.
Overtime wage rates rose 0.4 percent in the quarter and 1.9 percent in the year to March.
Salary and wage rate increases were seen in all nine major occupation groups. Within the professionals group (up 3.6 percent), there was an annual rise of 6.2 percent for teaching professionals.
SNZ noted the June quarter Labour Cost Survey would be the first since the minimum wage for employees aged 20 and over rose to NZ$7/hour from $6.375/hour on March 1.
It said the minimum wage rise may affect the index in coming quarters, particularly for hourly rates, as it is expected to have a flow-on effect above the minimum level.
